Mr. Bashir Uddin Zendigir with Mr. Md. Moniruzzaman Advocates ----- For the Petitioner.

Mohammad Yusuf Miah

full_judgment:
Md. Ashfaqul Islam, J: At the instance of the respondent-petitioner this rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 06.2.2003 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No.28 of 2003 by the District Judge, Chittagong admitting the appeal and staying the letter dated 23.01.2003 under Memo No. WA: PRA:/ CHITA :/ E.C. No.466/203(1) issued by Assistant Waqf Administrator, Dhaka removing the opposite party No.1 from the post of Motwalli and appointing the petitioner as Official Motwalli of E.C. No.466 Wali Miah Contractor Waqf Estate. Chittagong should not be set aside and/or to pass such other or further order or orders as this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The moot question that hinges in this revisional application is that whether Miscellaneous Appeal No.28 of 2003 before the District Judge, Chittagong is maintainable within the meaning of section 32(2) of Waifs Ordinance, 1962. 

 4. The opposite party No.1 herein on 6.2.2003 preferred a Miscellaneous Appeal No.28 of 2003 before the District Judge. Chittagong stating that on 24.1.1921 Wali Miah Contractor established a Waqf through registered deed No.124 and after his death his son Mohammad Hanif opposite party No.1 was appointed as Motwalli vide letter dated 23.5.1973. The step brother of the appellant-opposite party No.1 on 16.10.99 applied before the Waqf Administrator for appointing him as Motwalli and respondent No.2 allowed his application on 29.4.2001 when  the appellant opposite party No.1 preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No.123 of 2001 against the said order before the learned District Judge, who stayed said order of Waqf Administrator by his order dated 8.7.2001 in Miscellaneous Appeal No.123 of 2001. Respondent No.1 on 15.1.2003 applied before the respondent No.2 for appointing him Motwalli and accordingly respondent No.? on 23.12003 appointed the respondent No.l.as Motwalli without showing any cause upon the appellant. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the aforesaid order dated 23.1.2003 passed by the Waqf Administrator respondent No2 the opposite party ,No.1 .moved an appeal before the learned District Judge Chittagong which was admitted on 6.2.2003. 

 5. The respondent-petitioner being aggrieved by the order dated 6.2.2003 passed by the learned District Judge, Chittagong in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 28 of 2003 has invoked the revisional jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule. 

 6. Mr. Bashir Uddin Zendigir, appearing with Mr. Md. Moniruzzaman, the learned counsel for the petitioner after taking me through the impugned order dated 6.2.2003 passed in miscellaneous appeal by the District Judge and also the order of the Waqf Administrator respondent No.2 dated 23.5.1973 has taken a preliminary ground that the said miscellaneous appeal before the District Judge against the order of the Waqf Administrator respondent No.2 was not maintainable inasmuch within the meaning of proviso to section 32(2) of Waqf Ordinance 1996. Substantiating his contention the learned counsel took me through the relevant portion of the Ordinance and also the order passed by the respondent No.2 and other connected papers. In support of his contention the learned counsel placed reliance on two decisions of Appellate Division namely, the decision of Afsar Uddin Haider and another versus AM Mahiuddin and others reported in 5 BLC 83, and Tafijul Huq Sarker vs. Bangladesh and others reported in 4 MLR 19. 

 7. Mr. Mir Mahfuzur Rahman on the other hand, by filing a counter affidavit on behalf of the appellant-opposite party No.1 today in this Court has submitted that being confronted with the point of law as raised by the petitioner it is really difficult for him to rebut the same. But still the learned counsel relied on the case of Abul Hashem Taluked v. Administrator of Waqfs reported in 1 BLD 63 made his submissions for the purpose of bringing out the present case from the ambit of admitted position of law. 

 8. Be that as it may, I have heard the learned counsels for both the sides at length and gone through the impugned judgment as well as the revisional application, counter affidavit filed by the opposite party No.1 and other relevant papers appended to the revisional application in minute details. Mr. Zendigir the learned counsel for the petitioner has drawn my attention to Annexure-B of the revisional application which Is the application, filed by the appellant-opposite party No.1 before the District Judge in Miscellaneous appeal No.28 of 2003 praying for stay of the order of the Waqf Administrator dated 23.1.2003. 

 14. I have given my anxious deliberation on the issue and find substance on the preliminary submissions made by the Mr. Zendigir that on the facts and circumstances of the case and law governing the issue the miscellaneous appeal preferred before the District Judge, Chittagong was not maintainable. But in the context of decision reported in 4 MLR (A.D) 19 it seems that the remedy as sought for by the appellant in the Miscellaneous appeal before the District Judge is open to writ jurisdiction under article 102 of the Constitution. 

 17. The impugned order dated 6.2.2003 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No.28 of 2003 by the District Judge, Chittagong admitting the appeal and staying the order dated 23.1.2003 under Memo: No. WA: PRA/CHITA:/E.C. No.466/203(1) issued by the Assistant Waqf Administrator Dhaka is set aside.
